equation_request.abstract:
We show a perfect state transfer of an arbitrary unknown two-qubit state can be achieved via a discrete-time quantum walk with various settings of coin flippings, and extend this method to distribution of an arbitrary unknown multi-qubit entangled state between every pair of sites in the multi-dimensional network. Furthermore, we study the routing of quantum information on this network in a quantum walk architecture, which can be used as quantum information processors to communicate between separated qubits.

- 03.67.Ac, 03.67.Lx, 03.67.Bg, 03.67.Hk

specification.problem: Perfect state transfer of an arbitrary unknown two-qubit state between sites via a discrete-time quantum walk with coin flips; the abstract gives no explicit dynamics, so only a generic background framework and a tiny assumed instance can be specified.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest construction: a generic discrete-time coined quantum walk on a 4-site cycle, with the two-qubit state to be transferred encoded in a placeholder way. The paper's specific coin settings, multi-qubit entanglement distribution, multi-dimensional network and routing protocol are outside the scope.

coin operator at step t (coin setting)

symbols.domain: unitary on coin x position space

equations.label: Walk step
equations.description: Generic discrete-time coined walk with possibly step-dependent coin operators.
equations.justification: Abstract mentions a discrete-time quantum walk with various coin flippings; this is the standard form, not the paper's specific one.

equations.label: Shift operator
equations.description: Coin-conditioned shift on an N-site cycle with modular arithmetic.
equations.justification: Assumed 1D cycle instance; the paper's network geometry is not given in the abstract.

equations.label: Transfer condition
equations.description: Perfect transfer means the target sites hold the input state exactly for every |\psi\rangle, with the remainder in a state independent of \psi.
equations.abstract_quote: perfect state transfer of an arbitrary unknown two-qubit state can be achieved via a discrete-time quantum walk
equations.justification: The claim of perfect transfer for arbitrary states implies exact, state-independent transfer.
assumptions: The encoding of the two qubits into walk degrees of freedom is unspecified

equations.label: Fidelity
equations.description: Perfect transfer criterion in terms of fidelity.
equations.justification: Standard figure of merit for state transfer.

specification.initial_state: Unspecified in the abstract; assumed |\psi\rangle encoded in the walker's initial coin/position degrees of freedom at the source sites, remaining degrees in a fixed reference state.

steps.description: Encode the unknown two-qubit state at the source sites (encoding assumed).
Apply T walk steps with a chosen coin sequence and shift.
Check the perfect-transfer condition at the target sites.

assumptions: Tiny instance: N=4 cycle, which is not from the abstract.
Coin sequence, encoding and T are not specified by the abstract.
All equations are generic background or assumptions.
